music.title: 432 Hz Natural Tuning
music.bio: The alternative concert pitch that proponents argue resonates with the natural geometries of the body and the cosmos. Heard once you have heard it, it is hard to unhear.

music.title: 528 Hz — The Love Frequency
music.bio: One of the six original Solfeggio frequencies recovered from medieval Gregorian chant — the tone associated with transformation and the repair of DNA.

music.title: Snatam Kaur — Live Sacred Chant
music.bio: American Sikh devotional singer whose live kirtan recordings have made the Aquarian sadhana mantras accessible to a global audience.

music.title: Deva Premal — The Essence
music.bio: Sanskrit mantras set to slow, breath-paced arrangements. The most-listened mantra album of the modern era — a gateway for the Western ear into the sound traditions of the East.

music.title: Hildegard von Bingen — A Feather on the Breath of God
music.bio: 12th-century Benedictine abbess, mystic, polymath, and composer. Her plainchant — recovered and recorded across the 20th century — is some of the most haunting sacred music in the Western canon.

music.title: Arvo Pärt — Spiegel im Spiegel
music.bio: Estonian composer of sacred minimalism. Spiegel im Spiegel — Mirror in the Mirror — is eight minutes of piano and violin that have made more people cry than most films.

music.title: Bach — Goldberg Variations
music.bio: Thirty variations on a simple aria, originally written to soothe an insomniac count. Glenn Gould recorded them twice — at twenty-two and at fifty — and the difference between the two readings is itself a teaching.

music.title: Pink Floyd — The Dark Side of the Moon
music.bio: The album that turned a generation's interior life into music — time, money, madness, the moon. Forty-three minutes of pop philosophy with no equal.
